extraction.name: NWPU-RESISC45
extraction.description: A large-scale benchmark dataset for remote sensing image scene classification containing 31,500 images covering 45 scene classes with 700 images per class, featuring variations in translation, spatial resolution, viewpoint, object pose, illumination, background, and occlusion.
extraction.creator: Gong Cheng, Junwei Han, Xiaoqiang Lu (Northwestern Polytechnical University)
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Images were extracted by experts in the field of remote sensing image interpretation from Google Earth (Google Inc.), which maps the Earth by the superimposition of images obtained from satellite imagery, aerial photography and geographic information system (GIS) onto a 3D globe. Images were carefully selected under all kinds of weathers, seasons, illumination conditions, imaging conditions, and scales. Scene classes were selected by investigating existing datasets and searching keywords on Web of Science and Google Scholar.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Satellite imagery, aerial photography, and geographic information system (GIS) data accessed via Google Earth, covering more than 100 countries and regions all over the world.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Images were extracted by experts in the field of remote sensing image interpretation from Google Earth, carefully selected under all kinds of weathers, seasons, illumination conditions, imaging conditions, and scales.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Experts in the field of remote sensing image interpretation
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Almost all scene classification methods rely only on traditional remote sensing overhead imagery. Existing datasets have limitations including small scale of scene classes, small image numbers per class, lack of scene variations and diversity, and saturation of classification accuracy. Some scene classes (island, lake, mountain, snowberg) have lower spatial resolutions than others.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset enables intelligent earth observation and scene classification, with potential future integration of social media and spatial technology data (geo-tagged photos, GPS, Twitter) to improve 'what-is-where' mapping on Earth's surface.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for training, testing, and evaluating data-driven algorithms for remote sensing image scene classification, including deep learning-based methods. It serves as a benchmark for developing and evaluating new approaches to land use/land cover classification.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is freely and publicly available, released in 2016. No explicit versioning, update schedule, or deprecation policy is described.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Images were carefully selected under all kinds of weathers, seasons, illumination conditions, imaging conditions, and scales to ensure rich variations in translation, viewpoint, object pose and appearance, spatial resolution, illumination, background, and occlusion. Fine-grained scene classes with high semantic overlapping were added to increase within-class diversity and between-class similarity.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images were extracted from Google Earth by experts in remote sensing image interpretation. Each image was standardized to 256×256 pixels in RGB color space. Color histogram features were normalized to have an L1 norm of one. CNN features were extracted from specific layers (e.g., second fully connected layer of AlexNet yielding 4,096-dimensional vectors). BoVW codebook was generated via k-means clustering over all feature descriptors.

name.evidence: we propose a large-scale dataset, termed "NWPU-RESISC45", which is a publicly available benchmark for REmote Sensing Image Scene Classification (RESISC), created by Northwestern Polytechnical University (NWPU).

description.evidence: This dataset contains 31,500 images, covering 45 scene classes with 700 images in each class. The proposed NWPU-RESISC45 (i) is large-scale on the scene classes and the total image number, (ii) holds big variations in translation, spatial resolution, viewpoint, object pose, illumination, background, and occlusion, and (iii) has high within-class diversity and between-class similarity.
